transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm just... well, I've been struggling a bit lately. Um. I manage a retail store, so I'm used to being busy, but... recently things have felt a bit heavy. I guess what finally scared me into making this appointment is that I’ve been having these thoughts. Like... "If I didn’t wake up tomorrow, that might be easier." I don't want to hurt myself, it's just... it's just been hard.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these thoughts and feelings been ongoing, or have you felt like this before and it got better?

Um... I suppose it's been about six months now. Just this... low, flat feeling. It hasn't really gone away. I usually have my routines, things I do outside of the store... like morning walks, or this art class I was taking. But... I stopped. They just didn't do anything for me anymore. They didn't help. So, yes, it's been ongoing for a while.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or extremely confident — maybe even to the point where others noticed a change in you?

Um... I wouldn't say "high." But... before this slump hit, I suppose there was a stretch where I felt... I don't know, maybe almost too sure of myself. And... well, I guess I was getting irritated easily. I would snap at people over tiny comments. Like... my district manager questioned my store layouts, and I just... I got very short with him. I don't usually do that. But... that's about it.
Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt so energized or restless that you didn’t need much sleep, or when your thoughts were racing so fast you couldn’t keep up?
Um... no. I don't think so. I've always needed my sleep, even then. And... no, my thoughts weren't really racing. Just... normal, I suppose. I didn't notice anything like that.
Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had a time when you felt persistently low or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?
Um... no. Not that comes to mind. I mean... everyone has a bad week here or there, but... nothing like this. I've always just gone to work and... got on with it. So, no.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling down or losing interest in things before this current period?
No... I don't think so. I just... I haven't really had this happen before. Like I said, this is the first time I've felt this... stuck.
Have you ever had any other periods in your life, before this current one, where you felt persistently down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?

No, like I... like I just mentioned, I haven't. This is really the first time it's been like this for me. I've always just kept busy with the store and... well, pushed through. So, no, not before now.
Have you ever had any other times in your life, even before this current period, where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks?
No. I... I really don't think so. I mean, I'm pretty sure I already said that. I just... I don't have anything else to add about it. It's just this time.
Have you ever had any periods in your life before this one where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks, even if it didn’t last as long as this time?
I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again. No. I... I haven't. My answer is still no.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt unusually upbeat, excited, or hyper — not just happy, but almost to the point where it was out of character for you?

I guess... well, before this whole slump started, there was a time. I wouldn't say hyper, but... I just felt really sure of myself. Maybe too sure. And then I'd just... snap at people over little things. Like when the district manager said something about my store layouts, I just... I had no patience for it. But I wouldn't call it excited. Just... different.
Can you recall if there was a time when you felt abnormally upbeat or elevated, where you needed less sleep, were more talkative than usual, or had so many ideas that it was hard to keep track?

I don't know about being more talkative. But... I suppose I did have this burst of energy for a while. I just couldn't really sit still after work. I'd spend my evenings sketching out new store ideas... or reorganizing the shelves at my house. I think I even signed up for some extra training I didn't really need. I just... felt like I needed to keep busy, I guess.

Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt abnormally upbeat, elevated, or irritable — not just happy or excited, but noticeably different from your usual self — and if that lasted for several days in a row?

I don't really know. I didn't mark it on a calendar or anything. It might have been a few days... maybe a week. Like I said, I was just focused on getting things done. I didn't really keep track of how long it went on.

Can you recall if there was a time when you felt abnormally upbeat, energetic, or irritable — so much so that it was clearly different from your usual self — and this lasted for at least four days in a row?
I suppose it could have been four days. Like I said, I wasn't keeping track. It was just a period where I was busy. I don't know exactly how many days it was.

So, during that time when you felt more energetic and were doing a lot after work, was there a period of at least four days in a row where your mood was noticeably elevated or irritable — like you felt unusually good, overly confident, or easily annoyed — different enough that someone close to you might have noticed?

Well... I guess right before this current slump hit, there was a stretch. I just felt... I don't know, very sure of myself. Almost too sure. But then... I'd also just snap at people over little things. Like, if my district manager questioned one of my store layouts, I'd just get so annoyed. It wasn't like me to react that way.

During that time when you felt very sure of yourself and were snapping at people easily, did this mood last for at least four full days in a row — like a continuous stretch where you felt clearly different from your usual self?
I mean... I guess so. It probably lasted about that long. I just remember it being a continuous thing for a little while before I crashed. That's about all I can say for sure.

During that time when you felt very sure of yourself and were snapping at people easily, did this mood last for at least four full days in a row — like a continuous stretch where you felt clearly different from your usual self?
I thought I just said that. Yes, it was a continuous stretch. Probably four days, maybe a bit more. I wasn't exactly marking it down on a calendar, but... yes. It lasted a few days.

During that time when you felt very sure of yourself and were snapping at people easily, was there a continuous stretch of at least four full days where your mood was clearly different from your usual self — like you were noticeably more upbeat, irritable, or energetic in a way that stood out to you or others?
I... I don't know why we keep going over this exact same thing. I just answered that. Yes, it was a few days where I was acting differently. I really don't have anything else to tell you about it.

During that time when you felt very sure of yourself and were snapping at people, did you also experience at least three of the following: much more energy than usual, racing thoughts, being more talkative than usual, distractibility, doing things you wouldn’t normally do, or getting very little sleep without feeling tired?

I suppose... yeah, I had more energy. I just couldn't really sit still after my shift. I'd come home and... I don't know, keep sketching out ideas for the store displays, or I'd start reorganizing all the shelves in my own house. I even signed up for some extra training modules at work that I didn't really need to do. So... yes, I guess I was doing more than usual.

During that time when you felt very sure of yourself and were snapping at people easily, did you also experience at least two other changes like racing thoughts, being more talkative than usual, getting distracted easily, or doing things you wouldn't normally do?

I... I suppose I was easily distracted. I'd start setting up one of the displays, a planogram, and... I don't know, a customer would walk by with a bright scarf, or a song would come on the store speaker, and I'd just... lose my train of thought. Or a new idea would pop into my head and I'd go do that instead. So, yes, I guess I was distracted.

Or a new idea would pop into my head and I'd go do that instead. So, yes, I guess I was distracted.

opening_question.intent: Establish the patient's primary concern or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a current major depressive episode and a past manic episode lasting at least four days with elevated mood, increased energy, irritability, distractibility, and goal-directed activity. There is no evidence of prior depressive episodes, ruling out recurrent depressive disorder (F33.2). The manic episode is not severe enough to qualify for F31.3 (bipolar disorder, current episode manic severe), but sufficient for F31.4 (bipolar disorder, current episode manic moderate).
